questions.q: What is the purpose of this closing practice lab?
options: To introduce several brand-new Power BI features not covered earlier in the course
To apply every mechanism already covered in this course, yourself, in the order a real governance rollout follows
To replace the need for any of the previous 19 lessons
To test only Chapter 4's content in isolation
questions.explain: The lab is explicitly a structured walk-through reusing this course's existing concepts, applied hands-on in a realistic rollout order, rather than new material.

questions.q: In Part one of the lab, what should workspace roles look like, according to this lesson?
options: Everyone should be assigned the Admin role for simplicity
At least one person should have Viewer and one should have Contributor — not everyone as Admin
Only the tenant admin should have any role at all
Roles don't need to be set at all in a practice workspace
questions.explain: The lab specifically calls out setting real, differentiated roles — at least one Viewer and one Contributor — rather than defaulting everyone to Admin.

questions.q: According to Part two of the lab, what should happen before making a hypothetical change to a certified dataset?
options: Nothing — certified datasets can be changed freely with no review
Running impact analysis to see what the change would affect downstream
Deleting the dataset and starting over
Removing its certification first, then changing it, then re-certifying
questions.explain: The lab asks you to describe what you'd check in impact analysis before making a change — catching downstream breakage before it happens, consistent with Lesson 13.

questions.q: What three stages make up the deployment pipeline built in Part three of the lab?
options: Draft, Review, Published
Development, Test, Production — each backed by a real, separate workspace
Local, Staging, Global
Sandbox, QA, Release
questions.explain: Consistent with Lessons 16 and 17, the lab's pipeline uses the standard three stages — Development, Test, and Production — each backed by its own real workspace.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what course comes next in the Data Governance career path after Power BI Governance?
options: Metadata Management & Business Glossary
Data Lineage & Impact Analysis
Cloud Data Governance: Azure & AWS
There is no next course — this is the final course in the path
questions.explain: The lesson's closing section names Cloud Data Governance: Azure & AWS as the next course in the Data Governance career path, applying the same governance instincts to cloud platforms.
